messages:
sarah.k: Heads-up — seeing a spike of mTLS handshake failures from eu-west ingress starting ~12:10 UTC during the cert rotation. Errors show up as 495/handshake failed at the proxy layer. KMS decrypt errors for the ingress key also in logs. Opening thread to coordinate.
deploy-bot: Deployment event: cert-rotation-job finished for cluster eu-west-1 at 2026-03-20T12:09:54Z :white_check_mark:
sec-oncall: :warning: I saw the alert. Do we know which service account was used to request the new certs? Any RBAC changes pushed yesterday?
mike_r: Paste from proxy logs (redacted):

```
2026-03-20T12:11:02Z proxy[euw-1] ERROR handshake failed: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
2026-03-20T12:11:02Z proxy[euw-1] ERROR mTLS verify failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure
```

and KMS audit excerpt:

```
"protoPayload": {
  "methodName": "cloudkms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt",
  "status": {"code": 7, "message": "Permission denied"},
  "authenticationInfo": {"principalEmail": "infra-ingress-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}
}
```

jordan: That KMS error looks like AccessDenied (code 7). Did the key policy get restricted to a narrower principal or region-scoped key ring? We recently split keys per-region.
naomi: I rolled a small RBAC tighten two hours ago to remove long-lived access for some infra SAs, but I made an exception for infra-ingress-sa. Let me check the exact binding I pushed.
ops-eli: If decrypt is failing, TLS will fail if we can't unwrap private material. Suggest quick triage steps:
- confirm key resource name used by the ingress (KeyRing/Key/Version)
- check IAM bindings for that exact key
- search audit logs for successful decrypts earlier and failing attempts now
mike_r: Quick grep on the ingress config shows key name: projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/ingress/cryptoKeys/ingress-tls
naomi: I see the commit — I removed a group binding for `infra-ops@redwood.com` from the key IAM policy and added a conditional binding for US region SAs only. I forgot to allow the eu-west service account. My bad. Reverting now.
sec-oncall: Revert is reasonable. Before revert, can someone confirm there are no outstanding CVEs that prompted the change? We need to capture the reason in the incident notes (vuln triage) if this was intentional.
sarah.k: Reverting will likely restore KMS decrypts — but we also rotated certs. Two parallel actions to consider:
1) revert RBAC change -> allow decrypt -> ingress should be able to read current key material
2) if rotated certs are already issued to endpoints with new chain, we may need to re-issue or rotate back if there's mismatch
naomi: Revert pushed: IAM binding restored for `serviceAccount:infra-ingress-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Waiting for policy propagation (~30s).
deploy-bot: IAM policy update detected for resource projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/ingress :white_check_mark:
ops-eli: After propagation, test manual decrypt from control plane:
```
gcloud kms decrypt \
  --location=eu-west1 \
  --keyring=ingress \
  --key=ingress-tls \
  --ciphertext-file=/tmp/ct \
  --plaintext-file=/tmp/pt \
  --impersonate-service-account=infra-ingress-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
mike_r: Manual decrypt succeeded at 12:15 UTC. Proxy logs show subsequent successful handshakes starting 12:16 UTC. Initial error rates dropped back to baseline.
sec-oncall: Good. Next steps for postmortem / follow-up:
- create incident ticket and mark severity P2 while we root cause (link: https://redir/INC-2026-0347)
- vuln triage: capture whether RBAC change was in response to any advisory; add as artifact
- audit logging: ensure Cloud Audit Logs retention covers 90 days for key access events and export to secure bucket
- runbook: add explicit region-scoped RBAC checklist for KMS key changes and a preflight script to query impacted service accounts
jordan: Also recommend we add a quick test harness to validate ingress decrypts after IAM changes: a short CI job that impersonates the SA and attempts decrypt against a canary ciphertext.
naomi: I'll file the PR for the runbook and the CI test. Also will coordinate with security to review the RBAC tighten that motivated my change.
ops-eli: Add a small alert: if KMS Decrypt error count > 5 in 5m for any region, escalate to sec-oncall automatically. That would've flagged the issue faster.
sarah.k: Thanks all — restoring access + confirming decrypt fixed the handshakes. I'll draft the incident summary and link vuln triage notes. Tagging @sec-oncall and @naomi for follow-ups.
sec-oncall: Thanks team. We should schedule a short blameless postmortem tomorrow with infra, security, and oncall. Action items tracked in INC-2026-0347. :white_check_mark:
